quotes.text: Unlike his previous three albums, it is presented as a continuous mix hosted by producer DJ Smokey. Stylistically, the album has been described as a return to Skrillex's dubstep roots, featuring several previously unreleased tracks dating back to 2010.
Production was primarily handled by Skrillex himself, alongside Fred Again, Varg2TM, Whitearmor, and Eurohead, among others.
Vulture's Craig Jenkins praised the album's eclecticism, likening the album's mixtape format to Resident Advisor mixes and DJ Drama's Gangsta Grillz series.

Unlike his previous three albums, it is presented as a continuous mix hosted by producer DJ Smokey. Stylistically, the album has been described as a return to Skrillex's dubstep roots, featuring several previously unreleased tracks dating back to 2010.
Craig Jenkins praised the album's eclecticism, likening the album's mixtape format to Resident Advisor mixes and DJ Drama's Gangsta Grillz series.
This stuffed and gleefully self-aware 34-track LP is the sound of Skrillex, street cred enhanced, nostalgic for the drops that made him a star.

With slick, hairpin transitions throughout, it plays less like an album and more like an ultra-hype DJ mix. The project marks something of a return to form for the powerhouse US producer: after more than a decade of crafting pop hits and richly textured solo records, Skrillex, real name Sonny Moore, revisits the gnarly sound of early-'10s brostep that he helped create.
F*CK U SKRILLEX elevates Moore's signature sound while poking fun at its own cringe factor.

That's the era when Moore shaped the face of EDM with high-pitched lasers, whomping basslines and violent whirs like a UFO entering warp speed, all layered within the gargantuan drops that drove kids feral at Coachella. This maximalist aesthetic found its way into radio hits of the early 2010s.
Moore seems reflective of an earlier time on "ULTRA INTRO," which uses the same raging bass growls and stuttering clicks as Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites, Moore's intense yet humorous EP from 2010.

"MORJA KAIJU VIP" offers a slightly more rarified take on brostep: thanks to meticulous tinkering and newer studio tech, the electric screeches, revved-up drills and alien squelches sound cleaner. The mix is surprisingly spacious, the ears have more room to breathe.

Moore, who rose to fame as a vocalist in the Warped Tour poster band From First To Last, weaves an emo throughline into this cacophony, lending his own Auto-Tuned falsetto to tracks like "THINGS I PROMISED" and "VOLTAGE."

The diversity here is astonishing, if at times schizophrenic. Samples get recycled, chopped and screwed: Skrillex-flavoured Jersey club takes the stage on "REDLINE DASH." Moore, however, doesn't master every genre.
Yet the unexpected techno still works within such a propulsive album, which integrates dubstep, drum & bass, trap and dancehall by deftly alternating half- and double-time rhythms.

"KORABU" drops from dreamy pop into soft baile funk after Moore himself interrupts, saying, "give me, like, a trap beatbox. Half-time it." It's a sweet little window into his process, with a transition that flows beautifully.

Moore's style was always innovative, if poorly tuned, and certainly not for everyone. Now, elevated in service of a novel approach to album-making, it rises to meet the nostalgic moment for many of today's younger club kids and ravers who first heard electronic music when EDM made it radio-friendly in the early '10s.

Rather than leaning into his status as a commercial powerhouse to capitalize on his past successes, he takes that fame and power to the bank and uses it to buy state of the art electronic equipment and hire leagues of talented artists to work alongside him.

The album is presented as a seamless DJ Mix hosted by DJ Smokey (a fellow victim of meme culture) and is spread across 34 tracks. The tracks range from 30 seconds to 3 minutes and rarely ever present themselves as 'songs'.

The music is shattered and disparate. The second track "SPITFIRE" has the same structure as classic Skrillex tunes (verse/build/drop/repeat) but manages to accomplish everything in 90 seconds (Scary Monsters is 4 minutes in comparison). The last 30 seconds of the track are also almost entirely devoted to an incessant and un-danceable jittering.

Even with these short tracks, Skrillex is able to create some impressive constructions. "ANDY" begins with a classic R&B groove before transitioning into hype-infused EBM followed by chilled-out Pop and ending with a section as wholeheartedly resonant as it is blistering. "MIRCHI TEST" takes a single rhythmic idea and stretches it through different styles, intensities, and colors.

F*ck U Skrillex is perhaps best thought of as a work of pure integrity and ego. Skrillex is a complex artist with a complex legacy. It is hard to reconcile his massive success with his humble beginnings. He is a person who loves music and loves making music but also has a job to make music (this album came as a result of him wanting to get out of his record contract). To make music that sounds any one way is a disservice to himself. Therefore, to make something all-encompassing and mutated is the only way to create something truly personal.
